name: City Council Regular Meeting of May 16, 2023

APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF MAY 16, 2023

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Martin Herrera, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Marisol Cortez, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Alma D. Puente, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Richard Rojo, Councilmember/Authority Member – absent
  Julia Ruedas, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Councilmember Puente
  s) Councilmember Martinez Muela  6-0 (Councilmember Rojo absent)

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various legislative bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council will attempt to address and complete all
  Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. If the City Council completes
  all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the City Council will take a short recess
  and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m. In the event the City
  Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed Session items by 7:00
  p.m., the City Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end of the meeting,
  immediately following Council Communications. Should any member of the public wish to
  address the City Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the City Council shall
  allow such person to address the City Council on such matter(s) prior to going into Closed
  Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an agendized Closed
  Session matter shall (i) call-in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed on page
  1 of this agenda, above, prior to the City Council going into closed session; and (ii) be
  subject to a single speaker time allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total per
  speaker to address the City Council on any or all closed session items of business.

  Mayor Ancona invited members of the public to address the City Council on Closed
  Session Items 4.1 through 4.11. Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into
  Closed Session at approximately 6:01 p.m. Mayor Ancona and the City Council
  reconvened from Closed Session at approximately 7:07 p.m.

  Assistant City Attorney Lloyd Pilchen reported out of Closed Session with respect
  to Items 4.1 and 4.11.

5.  INVOCATION:  Chaplain. Chaplain Manny Coronilla, Calvary Chapel El Monte

  2
   City Council Meeting Minutes of May 16, 2023

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  Ayden White, 3rd Grade Student from Le Gore Elementary School.
  Present

7.  RECOGNITIONS, HONORS AND COMMUNITY INTEREST PRESENTATIONS:

  7.1  Presentation by the City Council to Ayden White from Le Gore Elementary School
  for Leading the Pledge of Allegiance. Present

  7.2  Presentation by the City Council Proclaiming the First Friday in June to be National
  Gun Violence Awareness Day. Present

  7.3  Presentation by the City Council Proclaiming the Month of May 2023 as American
  Asian and Pacific Islander Heritage Month. Present

  7.4  Presentation by the City Council to the El Monte Pee Wee Cheer All Cheer
  Captains. Present

8.  GENERAL PUBLIC COMMENT:

  This time has been set aside for members of the public to directly address the City Council
  on agendized items of business (other than those agendized as public hearing or closed
  session items) or on any other matter of interest to the speaker/caller that is within the
  subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing Authority, the Financing
  Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”). Each speaker/caller will
  be limited to a single allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total to address the Council
  on any or all matters covered by this section. As explained more specifically under the
  Public Hearing portion of this agenda, members of the public wishing to offer comment on
  items of business agendized under the Public Hearing portion of the agenda shall have a
  separate allotment of three (3) continuous minutes per speaker per public hearing item.
  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration
  at a future meeting. Persons wishing to address the Council on matters covered under
  General Public Comment shall call in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed
  on page 1 of this agenda, above, by or before the General Public Comment portion of the
  agenda is closed. The City Council shall be under no obligation to entertain comments
  from speakers/callers who submit cards or call in to speak on matters covered by the
  section after the General Public Comment portion of the agenda is closed.

  Eileen Penson – From the Public Library provided update regarding the free lunches being
  served during the summer at Norwood from June 5th to August 11th. Free for those ages
  18 and under.

  Jane Myring – Representing the Women’s Call. Thanked the City Attorney’s Office for
  paying their rent. Would like to request a written answer regarding why one organization
  is treated differently.

  Cindy Wu – Board Member Mountain View School District. Thanked the City Council
  regarding the Gun Violence Proclamation. Thanked the City Council for recognizing the
  month of May as American, Asian and Pacific Islander Heritage Month. Mountain View
  has a speech contest about what the younger people are thinking about areas of
  improvement at the City.

  Alyssa Garcia – Read her speech that she wrote for the Mountain View speech contest.
  Spoke about the positive things and the flaws that the City has.

  Leticia Marquez Hernandez – Here supporting her daughter Elisa Garcia for having the
  courage to speak out and come out of her comfort zone. Encouraged other parents to
  bring their kids to the City Council meetings.
  Julio Ramirez – Spoke about the last meeting about the 4th of July. Thanked
  Councilmember Martinez Muela for bringing this up. Spoke about gun violence.

  Mary Ann Powers – Have been dealing with the drought for many years it was a very
  convenient way to ignore the unkept yards. Now you see more unkept yards than kept
  yards. The City has to hold the landlords responsible.
  3

  Edward Sauceda – Spoke about public safety and the need for another bear cat.

  Jesse Fierro – Spoke about issue with one of his neighbors regarding a fence.

  Gabriel Ramirez – Made a suggestion to the City Council and Directors regarding having
  a CPR training. Also spoke about public records requests. Requested additional staffing
  to assist with complying with public records requests.

  9.1  Transmittal of the Treasurer’s Cash and Investment Report for the Quarter Ended

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

10.  DEMAND RESOLUTION NO. D-687

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF EL MONTE, CALIFORNIA,
  ALLOWING CERTAIN CLAIMS AND DEMANDS AND SPECIFYING THE FUNDS OUT
  OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO BE PAID.

  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF EL MONTE, CALIFORNIA, DOES RESOLVE AS
  FOLLOWS: SECTION 1. That the attached list of claims and demands totaling
  $4,442,798.40 have been examined by the City Treasurer and that warrant numbers
  1113805 through 1114215, and the payroll ending April 15, 2023, inclusive are hereby
  allowed in the amounts and ordered paid out of the respective funds as set forth.

  m) Councilmember Puente
  s) Councilmember Ruedas  5-0 (Councilmember Martinez Muela and Rojo
  absent)

11.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES: Regular Meeting Minutes of April 18, 2023; and Regular

  m) Councilmember Puente
  s) Mayor Ancona  6-0 (Councilmember Rojo absent)

12.  CONSENT CALENDAR:

  All matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine in nature and
  may be enacted by one motion approving the recommendation listed on the Agenda. One
  or more items may be removed from the Consent Calendar so that they may be discussed,
  considered, and voted upon individually by the Council. A matter may be removed from
  the Consent Calendar and taken up separately by way of a seconded motion of any
  member of the Council with the approval of a majority of the Council quorum.

  12.1  Waiver of Full Reading of Ordinance(s).

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Approval to waive full reading (except title) of all ordinances appearing on the
  City Council agenda as authorized under Government Code Section 36934,
  unless otherwise directed by the City Council.

  Total Cost: $133,350  Account No:  299-61-624-6111 - $83,350
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? Yes  100-61-611-6111 - $50,000

  s) Mayor Pro Tem Herrera  6-0 (Councilmember Rojo absent)

12.4  Consideration and Approval of a Third Amendment to Attorney-Client Agreement
  with Danning, Gill, Israel & Krasnoff, LLP for Bankruptcy Legal Services Relating
  to Illegal Cannabis Operations.

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Approve the Third Amendment to the Attorney-Client Agreement with Danning,
  Gill, Israel & Krasnoff, LLP, to increase the cap on legal fees from $75,000 to
  $95,000 incurred in the representation of the City of El Monte in the bankruptcy
  matter (Crown Estates Holding) involving property where illegal cannabis
  activities have occurred; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to make nonmaterial changes in consultation with
  the City Attorney’s Office and execute all implementing documents.

16.  CITY MANAGER’S AGENDA: None

17.  WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS: None

18.  COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS/REPORTS:

  18A.  Mayor Ancona

  18A.1 Discussion on Budget Workshop Date.

  Discussed having budget meetings June 12th and June 13th at 6:00 p.m.

  Mayor Ancona – Spoke about her trip to Sacramento for the State Police Officer’s
  Memorial. Also spoke about the National Memorial Ceremony that took place in
  Washington DC. There were over 400 fallen officers in 2022.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Roger Cobian was selected to sing the National
  Anthem at the memorial.

  18B.  Mayor Pro Tem Herrera

  18C.  Councilwoman Cortez

  18C.1 Update Regarding the El Monte RV Site Clean Up.

  Thanked the City Manager, City Attorney and staff for the work being done on the
  El Monte RV Site.

  6
   City Council Meeting Minutes of May 16, 2023

18D.  Councilwoman Martinez Muela

  Thanked staff for a beautiful breakfast for the National Day of Prayer. All the
  Chaplains were present. Mother’s Day at Farmers Market was tremendous. The
  flowers that Councilmembers got to pass out to the community was great. Spoke
  about and thanked everyone who put together the Insprire Event.

  18D.1 Update on Budget Workshops for the City Council.

  Spoke about this year’s Mid-Year budget and the use of $7.0 million from ARPA
  for this year. Some of the approvals that happened at the last meeting are going
  to adversely affect the City. Deeply concerned that all is okay but not everything
  is okay.

  Will the City Council receive the binder prior to the budget workshops.

  18D.2 Discussion on the Fair and Equitable Treatment of Nonprofit Organizations.

  Would like to understand how certain organizations have the $1.00 fee and how
  other organizations are paying a tremendous amount of rent.

  The City Council has requested a Policy regarding non-profit organizations
  regarding this.

18E.  Councilwoman Puente

18F.  Councilman Rojo

18G.  Councilwoman Ruedas

  18G.1 Status on the My El Monte Application Requests from the Community.

  Interested to know what is going on with the My El Monte Application Requests
  from the Community. What is the community asking, what are the needs?

  18G.2 Discussion Regarding Monthly Recognitions to Local Businesses.

  Attended the ribbon cutting ceremonies for two of the businesses. It would be great
  to recognize local businesses in the City.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Would like to bring back the Quarterly meeting
  that the City used to hold.

  Mayor Ancona – The Quarterly meetings will open up the space for the community.

  Mayor Ancona – Have we promoted that we have openings on our
  Commissions/Committees.

  posted no less than 72 hours prior to the start of the subject regular meeting. Although it

  supporting materials may render their website posting infeasible. Nevertheless, all
  supporting materials related to any item on this Agenda, that is made available to the
  members of the council may be inspected by members of the public at the City Clerk’s
  Office located at 11333 Valley Boulevard, El Monte, Monday through Thursday, 7:00 am
  – 5:30 pm. For more information, please call the City Clerk’s Office at 626-580-2016.

  All public meetings and events sponsored or conducted by the City of El Monte are held
  in sites accessible to persons with disabilities. Requests for accommodations may be
  made by calling the office of the City Clerk at (626) 580-2016 at least three (3) working
